elements.speaker: Speaker 1
elements.text: Good morning everyone, and welcome to the Future of AI conference. I'm the host of today's panel, and we have two wonderful guests who build intelligent audio systems.

elements.speaker: Speaker 2
elements.text: Thank you. Artificial intelligence is changing how machines understand sound. Ten years ago a computer could barely recognise a spoken word. Today neural networks can transcribe speech, detect sound events and even estimate the tone of a conversation.

elements.speaker: Speaker 3
elements.text: And I think the most exciting part is what comes next. Future technology will combine audio intelligence with spatial sound, so devices know not only what happened but where it happened.

elements.speaker: Speaker 1
elements.text: Let's talk about product planning. If you were designing an audio analytics product today, what would you build first?

elements.speaker: Speaker 2
elements.text: I would start with reliable transcription and semantic search. People want to ask where a topic was discussed and jump straight to that moment in the recording.

elements.speaker: Speaker 3
elements.text: For me it is anomaly detection. In a factory or a hospital, an unusual acoustic event can be the first sign that something is going wrong. Machine learning can flag those moments automatically.

elements.speaker: Speaker 1
elements.text: That siren outside is a good example. A smart system should recognise it as an event, not as part of our conversation.

elements.speaker: Speaker 2
elements.text: Exactly. Sound event detection separates speech from music, alarms, traffic and applause, and every event gets a timestamp on the timeline.

elements.speaker: Speaker 1
elements.text: Wow, that was loud. I think somebody dropped a glass at the back of the room. Is everyone okay?

elements.speaker: Speaker 3
elements.text: That is a perfect live demonstration of an acoustic anomaly. The energy and the spectrum changed suddenly, which is exactly what an isolation forest can detect.

elements.speaker: Speaker 2
elements.text: Looking ahead, I believe predictive analytics will matter most. If a system can forecast conversation activity, it can help moderators keep a meeting engaged.

elements.speaker: Speaker 3
elements.text: And privacy must stay at the centre. Running these models locally, on the device, means recordings never have to leave the room.

elements.speaker: Speaker 1
elements.text: Wonderful insights about artificial intelligence and the future of audio technology. Thank you both for joining us, and thank you all for listening.
